INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information.

2. When practising Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Comprehension.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: Poetry, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: Poetry.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: Poetry.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: Poetry.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: Poetry.

4. When practising Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility.

5. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.

6. In INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Only memorise without using the language
   B. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   C. Mix random languages with no purpose
   D. Avoid speaking to classmates

7. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency.

8. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.

9. When practising Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.

10. When practising Attentive Listening: Poetry, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening: Poetry.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening: Poetry.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening: Poetry.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening: Poetry.

11. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.2.1 Reading Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Public Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Narratives and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information.

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: Poetry.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting: Neatness and Legibility.

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.

6. B — Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency.

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening: Poetry.

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information.

12. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 7.2.1 Reading Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Public Speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 8.2.1 Extensive Reading: Narratives; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
